properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/06/2022 to INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC in Hepburn Twp, Lycoming county. 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/06/2022
Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 941156
Permit API: 081-21660
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Hepburn Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 1/06/2022
Comments: On January 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for a spill at the Inflection Energy Hensler Well Pad. On January 5, 2022, around 2140, Zac Subra reported a spill of approximately 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the well pad surface. At about 920 on January 6, 2022, DEP spoke with Zac Subra on the phone. Mr. Subra said a hydraulic fluid line on a water truck ruptured and caused the spill. Inflection contractors began removing the hydraulic fluid and excavating the impacted soil immediately. Inflection contractors excavated an area of about 20 ft. X 15 ft. of the pad surface. Due to the ground being frozen, Inflection contractors only had to scrape the top of the pad surface to remove the impacted soil in the previously noted area. The impacted soil was added to a rolloff dumpster and hauled to a landfill. Inflection then went back to the pad during the day to verify that the impacted soil had been completely removed. Zac said a small amount of remaining soil had to be removed at this time since it was not observed earlier in the morning. The small amount of soil was added to barrels and is awaiting approval to be disposed of. Inflection then backfilled the excavated area with clean fill. Photos of the area excavated and clean up were provided by Inflection Energy. The spill of hydraulic fluid outside of containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.54. The violations have been immediately corrected.

Comments: On 5/06/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-397312) at the Clara Jacques 1 well plugging site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows-up to IR 4186065, where violations were issued against severe tire rutting observed in the access road.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance along Five Forks Road (photos 1 and 2). An additional RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing. The RCE adjacent to the well plugging site is laden with sediment (photos 15 and 22). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photos 9, 12, 17, 19, and 20). Significant tire rutting remains throughout the access road. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. Well plugging equipment was observed on site, however plugging operations do not appear to be occurring at the time of inspection. A puddle with swirly rainbow sheen was observed adjacent to well plugging rig. This swirly rainbow sheen remained intact when disturbed, which is a known indicator of a petroleum-based release.The Department identified an access road cross-culvert at the time of IR 4186065 (photo 23). No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4186065 shall remain outstanding. Additional violations shall be issued for failure to adequately protect the cross-culvert shown in Photo 14 and for failure maintain the RCE adjacent to the well plugging site. Additional volations may be forthcoming against the swirly rainbow sheen released adjacent to the well plugging rig.

Comments: On 02/21/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/21/2024 Range Resources Representative, Derek Zofchak, reported an approximately 25 to 30-gallon release of reused water off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representatives, Derek Zofchak and Denny Furmanek, were on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Furmanek and Mr. Zofchak informed the Department that that the release was discovered today (02/21/2025) at 10:55 am, that the quantity released was approximately 25 to 30 gallons, and that remediation efforts had already begun on the impacted area. The source of release was determined to be damaged secondary containment. The secondary containment had been damaged by a truck tire and the fluids on containment overtopped the containment berm and continued off an adjacent duck pond and onto the pad aggregate. Conductivity probe calibrated on 02/21/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-The area impacted by the release was observed. The area appeared to measure approximately 150 ft in length by 35 ft in width. Pooled fluid with a sheen was observed throughout the area. The damaged secondary containment was observed. It was made known that a crew was on site to repair the damaged containment. A vac truck was observed on site removing pooled fluids in the impacted area and on containment (Photos 3-5).-Field conductivity screening was conducted immediately in front of a large, gray electrical box. Over Range (greater than 20 ms/cm) field conductivity readings were observed (Photos 6-8).-Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 7.21 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 9-12).-The extent of the impacts was observed where a non-elevated field conductivity screening of 1,432 s/cm was observed (Photos 13-14).-Remediation efforts were in progress at the time of inspection. Operators were observed scraping off impacted aggregates with heavy machinery (Photos 15-17).-A roll-off box arrived on site during the inspection. It was stated that the impacted material would be placed in the roll-off box and that waste manifests would be provided to the Department (Photo 18).Determination:Violations issued.

Violation ID: 8267124
Permit API: 111-20223
Unconventional: No
County: Somerset
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/10/2026
Comments: On March 10, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management's Neilan 1 well located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead. Attached to this wellhead was a small metal production tank, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this production tank either.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed some production equipment and a meter box on site. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this meter box or the production equipment attached to it.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right still had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time.The Department obtained soil conductivity readings at the base of the production tank near the corroded piping. Readings of 0.74ms, 0.42mS, 0.56mS, were obtained. These readings appeared elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading obtained of 0.09mS. It does not appear any remediation has occurred on site at the time of this inspection.Soil conductivity readings under the pipe were collected in the same localized location during the Department's previous inspection documented in IR 4106039 where it was 1.285mS. Therefore, since neither evidence of remedial actions were observed, nor a response from the operator has been received, the violations for a release remain outstanding as it appears the release may be diluting and/or migrating into the surrounding soil/subsurface areas.During IR 4106039, the Department requested the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of that inspection report. The written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, a plan for remediation of the spill or release, and how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requested the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon its receipt. To date, the Department has yet to receive the aforementioned documents.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from broken and corroded piping off of a production tank on site is remaining outstanding at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Permit API: 113-20482
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Elkland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/07/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of produced fluid. The release occurred at the frac tanks near the wells just to the northwest of the wells. At the time of inspection, the quantity of released produced fluid was unknown but was reported to be at least 1 barrel. I met onsite with Mike Deming, Expand. There were two sets of containment, each approximately 70' long by 55' wide. The staining appeared to be concentrated near the front-center of the tanks and between the two sets of containment for about half the length of the tanks. There were some holes identified in the offload area of the secondary containment shown in Photo 3. Soil conductivity was checked using a Groline soil conductivity meter. The damp areas/fluid were greater than 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) which is the upper limit of the conductivity meter. Expand indicated that the conductivity of a few puddles in these areas was around 21 mS/cm, having used a YSI meter. There were no other puddles on the pad surface or seeps found between the pad and the infiltration basins. The soil conductivity below the pad and in the basins ranged between 0.05 mS/cm and 0.68 mS/cm.The set of tanks in the foreground of Photo 1 are going to be cleaned and removed in order to pull the containment. Some of the tanks in the background of Photo 1 will also be removed and the containment lifted as much as possible to facilitate a full assessment and remediation of the impacted area. The remediation is tentatively scheduled to begin 7/9/25.Per a discussion with Mike Deming, the site will be remediated under Act 2 requirements. The result of this inspection is Violations noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). There are also outstanding violations for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a) due to a release documented in inspection 3981577 from 5/20/25 and inspection 3982600 from 5/22/25. The release detailed in those inspections is also undergoing Act 2 remediation. The violations may be closed after the completion of Act 2 remediation.

Comments: On July 11, 2023, inspection conducted at the Rumpelstiltskin well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Present were myself, EQT representatives David Crayne and Carey Vallor-Bell, and Moody representative Jona Stoskey. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred on July 10, 2023 at 2:35 PM, and was reported to the Department the same day at 4:27 PM by DJ Hardy. The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Hardy while en route to the pad, who explained that a GPU dumpline failed and spilled approximately one barrel of brine fluid onto the ground. He also stated that the area behind the unit was excavated, but impacted soil remains around and under it. The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP was onsite (see photo 2). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable with no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 3 and 4). Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-23
Comments: On 12/19/19 a malfunction with the GPU occurred, causing the vessel to explode. On 12/20/19 OGI Joel Keller conducted inspection 2974755 and noted soil staining and a damp appearance. OGI Keller requested a follow up inspection be conducted by a WQS. On 12/23/19 at approximately 0800 I conducted a follow up inspection. The temperature was well below freezing at the time of inspection. Upon arriving at the explosion location I observed water on the access road that was not frozen, despite the freezing temperature. A soil conductivity probe was utilized and a reading od 12.02mS was observed (see photograph). Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed throughout the access road and on the east side of the access road. Trees and shrubs on the east side of the access road appeared wet. The liquid was not frozen and appeared to be brine, as further demonstrated by elevated soil conductivity readings in the area. No other trees or shrubs appeared wet, except for those east of the GPU location where elevated soil conductivity was observed. Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed further North toward the well head on the east side of the access road (see photographs). Elevated soil conductivity readings were also observed adjacent to brine tank 2. The highest reading observed was 12.83mS. Both brine tanks were severely corroded and brine tank 2 exhibited a large hole (see photographs). Brine tank 1 exhibited several smaller holes that appeared to have occurred due to shrapnel from the GPU explosion. The gravel in the former GPU location appeared to be stained, but the soil conductivity was not elevated. The Department recommends the visually impacted material is removed. Soil sample 3402-076 was collected from an area exhibiting elevated soil conductivity. Soil sample 3402-077 was collected from an area on the northwest portion of the site in an area that appeared to be unimpaired with low notably lower soil conductivity (see photographs). The Department recommends the spill is addressed consistent with the Act 2 process.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/17/2026
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to the observation of production fluid exiting the secondary containment of the Lot 740 tank battery. Conventional well Lot 740 15 (API # 123-47075) is nearest the tank battery. The conventional well appears to be plumbed for production. An old sign displaying the API number, well name, and the wrong operator contact information is posted on a tree near the location. The sign should be updated with the current operator's name and contact information. The tank battery at the site has 2 steel tanks and a separator situated within an earthen secondary containment. The secondary containment was approximately 60ft x 20ft. Evidence of staining, dead vegetation, numerous deer tracks, and conductivity readings over range (greater than 20,000 mS/cm maximum that field meter can measure) were present in standing water throughout the entire secondary containment. This would indicate a large volume of production fluid filled the entire containment at one time (see photo 1). At the time of the inspection, the ground within the secondary containment was saturated with production fluid with some ponding throughout. A small amount of crude oil was also identified within the escaped production fluid. A containment drain inlet was located at a low point in the front left corner within the containment. A conductivity reading of 17.17 mS/cm was measured at the drain inlet (see photo 2). The ponding production fluid was flowing into the drain's inlet, exiting the containment through the drain outlet located at the exterior front left corner of the secondary containment (see photo 3). The containment drain was open and unattended at the time of this inspection. Sample 001 was collected at 13:10 at the containment drain outlet for further testing. A conductivity reading was also taken at this location measuring over range (see photo 4). The production fluid flowed from the containment drain into the road ditch traveling south approximately 50 feet (see photo 5). The escaped production fluid also flowed north in the road ditch approximately 10 feet before entering a road culvert where it continued westward into the woods for approximately 150 feet (see photo 6). The vegetation in the path of flow was dead, the ground was muddy and imprinted with deer tracks, and the conductivity readings measured high throughout the entire length of travel. The conductivity was measured near the apparent end of impact with a reading of 8.51 mS/cm in a puddle.The containment drain is required to be closed when unattended and the regulations state that any discharge is to only consist of precipitation that accumulates inside the containment, not production fluids. On June 18, 2026 a phone call was made to the operator, John McCool, in which he stated his intentions to work towards achieving compliance. He explained that the fluids currently stored in the tanks will be pumped empty and examined for leaks. If any leaks are identified, the tanks will be repaired or replaced. An excavator will be used to remove the contaminated soil within the secondary containment and beyond the containment drain exit following the path of travel through the woods. Upon disposing of the contaminated soils at an approved facility, a copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department. Confirmatory sampling will be required to confirm the impacts from the release have been sufficiently remediated. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites and Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/11/2024
Comments: On 9/11/2024, I conducted a follow-up inspection of the Kentor Well Pad following violations issued on 9/9/2024 for a produced fluid spill proceeding the plugging of the Kentor 8H Well (Inspection ID: 3826729, Enforcement ID). Staining as a result of produced fluid spilling onto the Kentor Well Pad was discovered on 9/6/2024 following the removal of secondary containment used in the Kentor 8H Well plugging process. Leatherwood LLC was the Operator responsible for the spill, however EQT took responsibility for spill remediation. EQT is following Act 2 cleanup protocols as it is still unknown how much produced fluid was spilled.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI and Moody and Associates. I spoke to SPSI who confirmed that the spill had originated from the secondary containment during the Kentor 8H well plugging process, however it was still unclear how much produced fluid was spilled. A hole dug near the beginning of remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well yielded in produced fluid seeping into the hole. At the time of inspection, I observed produced fluid sitting within the excavated hole. SPSI stated that they were waiting for the arrival of Moody and Associates to proceed with remediation because the origin of the remaining produced fluid was unknown.While on site I observed the following:-Leatherwood LLC and EQTs Act 9 signs were posted at the site entrance (Photos 1-2).-Discoloration in the aggregate on site was apparent where excavation and impacted material remediation occurred (Photos 3-4).-The hole excavated by SPSI early in remediation was still seeping produced fluid at the time of inspection. It was undetermined where the produced fluid was seeping from and how much remained on site that was unaccounted for. I observed high conductivity of the fluid sitting in the hole (9.20 mS/cm), and the soil below the fluid was slightly elevated but below 3 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).-Previously stained aggregate located approximately 15 feet from the excavated hole demonstrated normal conductivity, and the top layer of aggregate appeared to be scraped off (Photo 12).-The plugged Kentor 8H well was barricaded by concrete barriers and backfilled since previous inspection. I observed normal conductivity readings in areas around the concrete barriers that were previously elevated (Photos 13-18).-Rolloff boxes were staged on site with impacted material. Boxes were being hauled off site at the time of inspection (Photo 19).-A ditch installed left of the plugged well was holding rainwater at the time of inspection (Photo 20).Because an unaccounted amount of produced fluid is still seeping from the Kentor Well Pad into the excavated hole approximately 75-100 feet from the origin of the spill, violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54 and SWMA 301 remain outstanding. Additionally, The Department is requesting a copy of the Kentor 8H well plugging secondary containment plan and all maintenance and inspection records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

Comments: On 11/17/23 an incident inspection of the Coastal Greene Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 11/17/23. Background:On 11/17/23 Greylock self-reported a brine release on the Coastal Greene Well pad. On 11/17/23 I spoke to Keith Eighmey of Greylock to acquire additional details about the spill. During the inspection it was determined that an estimated 10-15 barrels of impaired water had been released to the pad surface from a failure of the 8MH GPU unit. Investigation showed that the release was contained to the pad area and no water ways were impacted. Mr. Eighmey said that Greylock would have equipment, a containment, and a roll off box on site by 1-2pm on 11/17/23. Findings:-An act 9 sign was present at the entrance to the well site (Photo #1).-The spill is suspected to have originated from the 8MH GPU units (Photo #2,6).-Standing water and a wet spot was observed around the GPU units (Photos #2,3,5,6,8,9).-Elevated conductivity was observed in standing water around the GPU units (Photo #4,7). -Crews were present on-site working to repair the GPU units. (Photos #2-6). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area.No impacts to WoC were observed. Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 78a54, and 78a64(a)b are being issued for the release of brine to the ground and failure to have the GPU units in secondary containment for a well drilled in 2018.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHIEF OIL & GAS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/01/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 945994
Permit API: 015-23674
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/22/2022
Comments: Samuel Louderback (DEP Geoscientist) and I took electrical conductivity (EC) readings from pooled liquid and soil of the pad surface, which ranged from 0.60-7.7 mS/cm. We used Oakton meters for the liquid, and Hanna soil probes for solids. Readings were mostly >2.0 across the majority of the pad surface, with generally higher readings on the north end of the pad. Liquid in the NE basin is 1.5 mS/cm, and 0.60 mS/cm in the SE basin. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation during this inspection. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Violations for an apparent brine release will remain open. The DEP recommends removal of pooled liquid with relatively high (>1.0 mS/cm) EC from the pad surface, wheelie trailer containment, and the NE basin. Air temp 44F JLP
